title.narrative: Strengthening Rural Governance for the Right to Adequate Food - Zimbabwe

description.narrative: Direct target groups: Rights holders at the micro- and meso-levels in the intervention areas; Members of Grassroots, Community-based organisations (CBO) and Civil Society Organizations (CSO) at the micro- and meso-levels: XX – (included in the total number of rights holders indicated above); Leaders of these organizations and paralegals; Members of CSOs at the national level; Staff of the civil society partner organizations in this program; Intermediaries such as journalists, academics, human rights institutions; Duty bearers at the micro- and meso-levels in the intervention areas; Duty bearers at the national level; Government representatives (including from donor countries) involved in international processes and staff of international bodies, organizations, and platforms.Indirect target groups: Population of the intervention areas (ca. 200.000 people) who will be reached through community awareness raising, multipliers in CBOs, dialogue events and media campaigns as well as benefitting from the improvement of public services.

Overall objective (impact):Progressive governance for the right to food, guided by the principles of participation, transparency, accountability, non-discrimination, and rule of law, for improved food and nutrition security in rural communities.Program objective (outcome):Duty bearers in the program countries (Kenya, Malawi, Ethiopia, Zimbabwe) progressively enact and implement inclusive legal frameworks, policies and programs that are conducive to the realization of the right to food and that promote accountability.

The global program "Strengthening Rural Governance for the Right to Adequate Food" (Phase 2) aims to raise awareness and strengthen decision-makers from politics, administration and traditional structures in the project regions so that they can better meet their responsibility for realizing the right to food. Community members in rural regions of these countries as well as civil society organizations are to be sensitized and supported in holding duty bearers accountable for the right to food and entering into dialogue with them in order to achieve improvements. The program pursues a multi-level approach that links the micro level (communities and villages) with the meso level (districts, provinces) and the macro level.
